_note: LEVEL 4-32's DARK DRAGON - entity `dark_dragon.ent`, spawned by `dark_dragon_spawn`,
role `boss_spawn`. The fourth boss, the last level of the game, and the last thing in
this remaster.
THE WHOLE LEVEL, decoded end to end, because every piece of it is one mechanism:
1. level31c is `darkest` and holds an unlit torch (`light_off`, 210 34). Shooting it
lights it - which takes the LIGHT WALL away (Torch.hpp, already built) and, in the
same act, adds a `light_from_projectile.ent`.
2. `dark_dragon_spawn` waits 3000 ms, sees that light, and marks ITSELF destroyed.
3. 4000 ms later it adds `dark_dragon.ent` at its own place, calls
breakDarkDragonWall, starts the music, and deletes itself.
4. The dragon hovers in, settles at `fighting`, and shoots fireballs at the player.
5. The player portals the BARREL BOMB - `teleportable = 1` - into the line of fire.
The dragon's own fireball detonates it, and the blast BURNS the dragon.
6. Each wound: hp -1, a red flash, YOUR PORTALS ARE TAKEN AWAY, it shoots out the
TORCH, and it restocks the barrel bomb.
7. At hp 0 it falls and drops a YELLOW KEY at `key_pos` and a platform at
`platform_pos`. The key opens the yellow door, and the door is the way to the exit.
THE BOSS SUPPLIES BOTH ITS OWN AMMUNITION AND ITS OWN DETONATOR, and that is not a
reading - addEntityIfItCantBeFound restocks `barrel_bomb` after every shot it takes, and
the port's own fireball path (Game.cpp) already asks an overlapping bomb to go off. The
level places no fire agent and no fire diamond, so the dragon's fireball is the ONLY
thing in level31c that can light the only thing that can hurt it.
THE LEVEL, measured from level31c.tscn: 768 x 256 px (`max` at (768, 256)) - an arena,
where level31a's dragon had 2632 px to chase you down. main_char (710, 48), door.ent
(704, 176), dark_dragon_spawn (-144, 210) off the left edge, shout (-4, 140), fighting
(16, 56), breakable_wall (32, 128), light_off (210, 34) with switch = 1, light_wall.ent
(64, 240), key_pos (78, 208), platform_pos (160, 240), barrel_spawn (430, 0),
barrel_bomb (430, 63), keyhole.ent (592, 200) yellow, door_locked.ent (624, 160) yellow.
properties: darkest = 1, no_music = 1. NO auto_camera - that is level31a's alone.
ETHCallback_dark_dragon_spawn, bytes 388631..389418. Two arms on isDestroyed(), which
(MiscCallbacks 347456..347560) is nothing but a `destroy` custom uint - destroy() sets
it and deletes nothing.
NOT destroyed:  elapsedTime > 3000 && SeekEntity("light_from_projectile.ent") != null
-> destroy(this); elapsedTime = 0
destroyed:      elapsedTime > 4000 && !isFinished
-> AddScaledEntity("dark_dragon.ent", spawnPoint.GetPosition())
breakDarkDragonWall(); playGameMusic(true)
playDarkDragonAppearSound(); DeleteEntity(this)
WHAT THE PORT WATCHES INSTEAD, and why it is the same event. The light entity is added
by ETHCallback_light_off (467198..467878): while unlit the torch spins and calls
hasProjectileAround(pos, 24), and a projectile within that adds
`light_from_projectile.ent`. That is exactly the condition Torch already decodes and
already counts - Torch::State::lit - so the port reads `lit > 0` rather than modelling
an entity whose only purpose is to be sought by name.
ONE DIVERGENCE, STATED: Torch is a TOGGLE, and `lit` here is monotonic - it counts
torches lit over the level's life and never comes back down. So a player who lit the
torch and shot the flame out again within the 3000 ms window would, in the original,
leave no light for the marker to find and disarm the summon; here the arming stands.
Recorded rather than built: it is a three-second race against oneself, in a level whose
torch is also the only way to see, and a port that modelled it would have to model the
light entity's own lifetime, which nothing else in the game reads.
breakDarkDragonWall (398405..398575) seeks `breakable_wall` and calls destroy on it.
level31c's breakable_wall_2217 carries metadata/breakable = 1, so it is ALREADY a
Demolish::Breakable with a body the port tracks - the removal goes through Demolish
exactly as the torch's light wall does, and the two are different bodies that never
meet. This level is the only one in the game that holds both kinds of wall.
dark_dragon.ent, read from the extracted entities (never copied here): type 0,
static 0, shape 2, sensor 1, density 0, gravityScale 0, Collision Size 220 x 220, and
custom data carrying `burnable`.
A SENSOR WITH NO SOLID BODY, so it cannot touch the player and the player cannot stand
on it - the ghost's shape, and the reason this module keeps a position rather than an
entity. It is also why the port tests the blast against it explicitly: Fire::Blast
matches candidates by body, and this boss has none, exactly as Game already does for
the ghost against a fireball.
`burnable` is what makes the barrel bomb the weapon. The blast's own filter is
isBreakableOrExplosiveOrBurnable, so the dragon is in the set it grabs.
radius_px is HALF of the 220 x 220 Collision. The original grabs with a sphere of
blast.radius_px against that real box; the port tests a distance against this radius
plus the blast's own, which is the same test with the box approximated by its half
extent. hp is NOT in the .ent - the callback writes 3 on its first tick.
ETHCallback_dark_dragon, bytes 389418..397662 - 8.2 KB and ~2178 instructions, the
largest callback in the game. States: APPEARING 0, FIGHTING 2, DAMAGE 3, DYING 4.
THE FIRE INTERVAL SHORTENS AS IT IS HURT, tested every tick against the live hp:
if (hp <= 2) fireInterval -= 600;  if (hp <= 1) fireInterval -= 600;
so 4200, then 3600, then 3000. It gets faster exactly as you get closer.
FIRING, when elapsedTime > fireInterval and !isFinished: GetClosestContact(dragon ->
char), and the shot happens only if the closest thing is the character - the same sight
gate as level31a's dragon, and asked the same way round here for the same reason
(Shot::FirstBody cannot return a capsule; dragon.json carries that decode). The muzzle
is scale(95) along the aim, addFireball carries killMainCharacter, and each shot brings
startEarthquake(15) and the barrel restock.
computeDarkDragonAngle (398213..398405) is getAngle(normalize(charPos - dragonPos)) +
PIb * 1.2 - and the follower it feeds smooths an ANGLE, not a position: the angle is
put in x, and read back as radianToDegree(follower.getPos().x). PIb is the inferred
PI/2 gravitywell.json records. The port aims along the segment the sight gate already
tested, as level31a's dragon does, and does not reproduce the angle arithmetic.
HURT ONLY BY FIRE, exactly as the ghost is: isBurned(dragon) -> DAMAGE, hp -1,
healBurn, playDarkDragonDamageSound. burn/isBurned/healBurn (419710..420017) are a
plain `burned` custom uint.
Seven waypoints, with shoutMove = scale(8, -32). A WaypointManager's hold on waypoint
i is the time to travel from i to i+1, so the path is:
spawn            -> shout             2500 ms   smoothBothSides
shout            -> shout                0 ms
shout            -> shout+shoutMove   1000 ms   smoothBeginning
shout+shoutMove  -> shout+shoutMove   1000 ms   smoothEnd
shout+shoutMove  -> shout+shoutMove    700 ms   smoothBeginning
shout+shoutMove  -> fighting          2200 ms   smoothEnd
fighting                                 0 ms   (terminal)
7400 ms in all. At waypoint 0 past bias 0.2 it calls startEarthquake(10), and its
frame is clamp(uint(smoothBeginning(bias) * 14), 0, 3) with the particle system and
playDarkDragonOpenMouthSound on frame 0. The port interpolates the path LINEARLY and
records the easing rather than applying it: what the position is for is the blast test
and the muzzle, and smoothBeginning is not decoded anywhere in this port.
A fresh WaypointManager with shoutMove = scale(32, -32): (currentPos, 1000), then SIX
at shout+move of 300 ms each alternating red and 3x-bright emissive, then (fighting, 0).
2800 ms in all. The emissive flash IS those waypoint colours, and it is presentation.
TWO THINGS IN IT ARE NOT PRESENTATION:
- PortalManager::killAll, at the moment it is wounded. Every portal you have placed
is taken away. In the port that is placed.clear() and flight.reset(); the budget and
portalsUsed are deliberately left alone, because killing portals is not a refund.
- At the LAST waypoint it seeks `light_off.ent` and, if it finds one, fires a fireball
at it. IT SHOOTS OUT YOUR TORCH. In a `darkest` level the torch is the light and,
through Torch, the light wall - so wounding the boss costs you the room's light and
the way you made it. That is the first time in the whole game `darkest` is a
mechanic rather than a colour, and it is why this level places a torch at all.
Then elapsedTime = 0 and state returns to FIGHTING.
Entered from any arm the tick hp reaches 0 and the state is not already DYING: the
boss music stops, playDarkDragonDeathSound, and a fresh WaypointManager with
fallMove = scale(32, -64):
currentPos                    -> shout+fallMove          3000 ms
shout+fallMove                -> shout+fallMove+(0,256)  6000 ms
(terminal)
and darkDragonOvertimeSmallExplosionAdder every tick (397662..398213: a random
direction, scale(64) * (randF(0.7)+0.4), an over-time small_explosion_no_light.ent -
presentation).
AT THE LAST WAYPOINT it adds key.ent at `key_pos`, a ghost_utility_spawn.ent with it,
single_block_plat_no_emissive.ent at `platform_pos`, calls explode, and deletes itself.
THE KEY IS THE LEVEL'S LOCK. level31c places keyhole.ent and door_locked.ent both
`yellow` and places NO key of its own - so the only key in the level is the one this
boss drops, and the fight IS the lock, exactly as it is for the ghost in level31b. The
colour is carried here because the key is created at run time and so has no node to
read it from.

not_built: Every sound: the appear, open-mouth, damage and death sounds, playGameMusic and the
boss-music stop. sounds.json already names the family.
The pictures and the shake: the 4-frame animation and its particle system, the emissive
flash (red and 3x bright), the scattered small_explosion_no_light.ent, explode's own
burst, and startEarthquake at 10 on entry and 15 per shot.
The neck bob: neckAdjustBias = min(neckAdjustElapsedTime / 2000, 1), h = scale(18), and
yOffset = (smoothBothSides(clamp((365 - angle)/25, 0, 1)) * 2 - 1) * h * bias, written
to `originalPos`. It moves the drawn head, not the boss.
THE PLATFORM THE DEATH ADDS, and this one is a GAP rather than a flourish. The original
adds a single_block_plat_no_emissive.ent at `platform_pos` (160, 240) as the dragon
falls. This port cannot: LevelBuilder::BuildEntity builds a node the scene holds, and no
node stands at that marker - the original makes the body from the .ent itself. There is
deliberately no flag for it in DarkDragon::Turn, because a flag Game could not act on
would be a hole shaped like a check. THE RISK, said plainly: the key drops at (78, 208)
and the keyhole is at (592, 200), so if that platform is the only way back across, the
level may not be finishable without it. Nothing in the data settles that - it needs the
level played. Building it needs a way to place a body from an .ent with no node behind
it, which is the same shape as LevelBuilder::BuildRigidCircle and is its own step.
ghost_utility_spawn.ent, added beside the key on death: the same utility marker the
ghost's restock path uses, and nothing in this port reads one.
addFireball's 2.0 fourth argument, undecoded in meaning here as in ghost.json.
